# Regenerating `public/og.png`

The social card is a committed 1200×630 raster. This file is how it was made and how to remake it.

## Why it is not generated by `npm run build`

Rasterising text needs a font rasteriser — `sharp`, `resvg`, `satori`, `canvas`, or a headless
browser. Every one of those is a heavyweight dependency, or a browser download, added to a project
whose entire production dependency list is five packages. The card changes when the dataset is
re-scraped, which has happened once. Paying a permanent build dependency for that is the wrong trade.

So the card is drawn with the Canvas 2D API in a browser, once, and the PNG is committed.

## The compensating control

Freezing counts into pixels is exactly the drift problem this codebase argues against elsewhere. The
guard is `src/data/og.test.ts`: it asserts the numbers drawn into the card still match the dataset,
and that `og:image:alt` restates the same numbers. Re-scrape the dataset and the suite fails, naming
what to redo. Do not delete that test in order to make a build pass.

## Recipe

1. `npm run dev`, open the app.
2. Paste the script below into the browser console. It draws the card and downloads it.
3. Replace `public/og.png`.
4. Update `BAKED_INTO_OG_IMAGE` in `src/data/og.test.ts` and `og:image:alt` in `index.html`.
5. `npm test` — all three assertions in `og.test.ts` must pass.

Fonts come from the system stack, matching the app's no-webfont rule. The card will therefore render
with Segoe UI on Windows and Helvetica on macOS. That is acceptable for a raster generated once; if
it ever matters, name a specific family here rather than leaving it to chance.

```js
(() => {
  const W = 1200, H = 630;
  const c = document.createElement('canvas');
  c.width = W; c.height = H;
  const x = c.getContext('2d');
  const BG='#0B0C10', PANEL='#1F2833', TEXT='#C5C6C7', CYAN='#66FCF1', TEAL='#45A29E';
  const SANS = '-apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif';

  // Flat fills only. A full-bleed 60px grid cost 75 KB in PNG, because every
  // antialiased hairline defeats the row filters.
  x.fillStyle = BG; x.fillRect(0,0,W,H);
  x.fillStyle = PANEL; x.fillRect(0,0,W,8);

  const axisY = 495;
  x.strokeStyle = PANEL; x.lineWidth = 2;
  x.beginPath(); x.moveTo(70, axisY); x.lineTo(W-70, axisY); x.stroke();
  x.strokeStyle = TEAL; x.lineWidth = 3; x.beginPath();
  for (let px=70; px<=W-70; px++){
    const t = (px-70)/(W-140)*40;
    const v = Math.cos(t*1.6)*Math.exp(-t/90)*Math.cos(t*0.31) + 0.35*Math.sin(t*2.9);
    const py = axisY - v*58;
    px===70 ? x.moveTo(px,py) : x.lineTo(px,py);
  }
  x.stroke();

  x.fillStyle = CYAN; x.font = `600 21px ${SANS}`;
  x.fillText('O P E N   P R O B L E M S   A T L A S', 70, 112);
  x.fillStyle = '#FFFFFF'; x.font = `700 72px ${SANS}`;
  x.fillText('Every unsolved problem', 70, 212);
  x.fillText('in mathematics, tracked', 70, 292);
  x.fillStyle = CYAN; x.fillRect(70, 336, 110, 4);

  x.font = `500 29px ${SANS}`;
  let sx = 70;
  // Update these four pairs from the dataset, not from memory.
  for (const [n,label] of [['591','tracked'],['478','open'],['105','solved'],['8','partial']]){
    x.fillStyle = CYAN; x.fillText(n, sx, 402);
    const nw = x.measureText(n).width;
    x.fillStyle = TEXT; x.fillText(' ' + label, sx + nw, 402);
    sx += nw + x.measureText(' ' + label).width + 32;
  }

  x.fillStyle = TEXT; x.font = `500 25px ${SANS}`;
  x.fillText('openmathproblems.kineticgain.com', 70, 578);
  x.fillStyle = '#79828F'; x.font = `400 19px ${SANS}`;
  const attr = 'Data: Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0';
  x.fillText(attr, W - 70 - x.measureText(attr).width, 578);

  const a = document.createElement('a');
  a.download = 'og.png';
  a.href = c.toDataURL('image/png');
  a.click();
})();
```
